_doc: Seed state hierarchy (knowledge_architecture.md section 4). Roots and siblings are tried in list order; the first whose predicate is true wins. Thresholds are percent of peak unless noted (parallel_fill, launch_frac are fractions). States over bank_conflicts / uncoalesced need a profiler that reports them; elsewhere classification stays at the parent.

states.mechanism: time is set by fixed latencies (launch/sync, or too little parallel work to hide memory latency), not by any throughput
most of the slot time is launch and synchronisation; fewer launches (batching instances, fusion, persistent kernels) is the lever
fewer work items than lanes: the machine idles; split the reduction/K dimension or give the grid more, smaller pieces of work
both memory and compute are near peak; only doing less work (fewer bytes and fewer operations) helps
time is set by bytes moved; fewer or cheaper bytes is the lever
the memory system moves many more sectors than the kernel uses: fix the access pattern before anything else
the op has reuse but the cache loses it; stage reused blocks explicitly in fast memory
streaming from DRAM near peak; only fewer bytes (fusion, lower precision, no redundant reads) helps
the busiest memory unit is on-chip (L1/shared/L2), not DRAM: bank conflicts, uncoalesced or redundant on-chip traffic
shared-memory accesses of a warp hit the same banks and serialise; pad or swizzle the tile
each byte is used about once (elementwise-like); only fewer bytes -- fusion, narrower types, no redundant passes -- helps
time is set by arithmetic issue; fewer or cheaper instructions, or faster units, is the lever
register use caps resident warps, so issue slots go unused while warps wait
dense multiply-accumulate at peak scalar issue; matrix units / register blocking change the ceiling
enough work but neither unit near peak: the kernel wastes issue slots or bandwidth (poor access pattern, low ILP, redundant work)
memory-side work dominates but bandwidth is unused: uncoalesced or narrow accesses, poor locality, too few bytes in flight
bandwidth is wasted on partially used sectors: remap threads to contiguous addresses
compute-side work dominates but issue is slow: dependency chains, low ILP, index math, no data reuse in registers
too few resident warps to hide latency (registers, shared memory or block shape limit residency)
registers per thread cap resident warps; cut live values or bound registers
a dense multiply-accumulate with enough reuse that runs far below peak: blocking for matrix units (or register blocking) changes the ceiling
